answer: Graph-based trust propagation restricts Sybil attacks by measuring transitive distance from verified seed nodes. Reputation spreads like an attenuating pigment across transaction edges, preventing colluding clusters from using an internal echo to fabricate legitimacy. To build influence, an attacker must conduct genuine exchanges with honest nodes, incurring non-recoverable capital costs per identity. However, this framework penalizes legitimate newcomers lacking an established on-chain relic.
